cards.name: Component
cards.description: Any documented code unit — services, handlers, utilities, hooks, UI components, stores. The universal building block of Paradigm.
cards.when: Always — every code unit you document gets a # prefix. If it's a file, function, class, or module worth naming, it's a component.

cards.name: Flow
cards.description: A multi-step process with ordered steps spanning multiple components. Documents the sequence of operations that accomplish a business objective.
cards.when: When logic spans 3+ components in a defined sequence. If steps must happen in order and involve multiple parts of the system, it's a flow.

cards.name: Gate
cards.description: A condition checkpoint that controls access to resources or operations. Defined in portal.yaml and enforced in middleware or route handlers.
cards.when: When a condition must be verified before proceeding — authentication, role checks, ownership validation, feature flags, rate limits. One responsibility per gate. Compose gates for complex condition logic.

cards.name: Signal
cards.description: An event that triggers independent side effects. Signals decouple the emitter from subscribers — the emitter doesn't know or care who listens.
cards.when: When an event should trigger side effects (emails, analytics, state updates) without the source needing to know about subscribers. Use signals for decoupled reactions.

cards.name: Aspect
cards.description: A cross-cutting rule with REQUIRED code anchors. Aspects enforce patterns across multiple components and must point to the actual enforcement code.
cards.when: When a rule or pattern must be applied across multiple components (audit logging, rate limiting, caching). Anchors are mandatory — no unanchored aspects allowed.

cards.name: paradigm_status
cards.description: Get project overview — symbol counts, project health, and available features. The orientation tool for new sessions.
cards.when: At the start of every session to understand the project state.

cards.name: paradigm_search
cards.description: Search for symbols by name, description, or tags. Supports fuzzy matching for typo tolerance.
cards.when: When you need to find a symbol but don't know its exact name or location.

cards.name: paradigm_navigate
cards.description: Navigate the codebase efficiently. Three intents: 'find' locates a symbol, 'explore' browses an area, 'context' discovers files for a task.
cards.when: Before reading files — use navigate for discovery, then read only the files you need.

cards.name: paradigm_ripple
cards.description: Show what depends on a symbol directly and indirectly. Analyzes the cascading impact of modifying a symbol up to N levels deep.
cards.when: ALWAYS before modifying any symbol. Non-negotiable. This prevents breaking downstream dependencies.

cards.name: paradigm_related
cards.description: Get all symbols directly related to a given symbol — what it uses and what uses it.
cards.when: When you need to understand a symbol's immediate connections without the full ripple cascade.

cards.name: paradigm_wisdom_context
cards.description: Get team wisdom — preferences, antipatterns, and architectural decisions — for specific symbols before implementing.
cards.when: Before making changes to any symbol, especially those with high fragility scores or complex history.

cards.name: paradigm_history_fragility
cards.description: Check stability scores and warnings for symbols. High fragility means frequent changes and rollbacks — proceed with caution.
cards.when: Before modifying symbols that might be unstable. Especially important for critical-path components.

cards.name: paradigm_gates_for_route
cards.description: Suggest which gates should be applied to a route based on existing patterns in the project.
cards.when: ALWAYS when adding a new API endpoint. Get gate suggestions before writing route code.

cards.name: paradigm_orchestrate_inline
cards.description: Plan and coordinate multi-agent task execution. Mode 'plan' returns suggested agents and cost estimate. Mode 'execute' returns full prompts.
cards.when: When a task affects 3+ files, involves security + implementation, mentions multiple features, or builds end-to-end.
cards.example: paradigm_orchestrate_inline({ task: 'Add JWT auth to user module', mode: 'plan' })

cards.name: paradigm_pm_preflight
cards.description: Run pre-implementation governance checks — verifies that planning steps (ripple, wisdom, gates) have been completed before coding.
cards.when: Before starting implementation on any task to ensure all preparation steps are done.

cards.name: paradigm_pm_postflight
cards.description: Run post-implementation governance checks — verifies that documentation, history recording, and validation are completed.
cards.when: After completing implementation to ensure all follow-up steps (purpose files, history, tests) are done.

cards.name: paradigm_flow_validate
cards.description: Validate flow definitions against the codebase. With checkImplementation=true, verifies gates exist, actions are implemented, and signals are emitted.
cards.when: After modifying flows or their constituent components. Use checkImplementation for deep verification.

cards.name: paradigm_aspect_check
cards.description: Verify an aspect has valid anchors and check coverage. Aspects REQUIRE code anchors — this tool validates they exist and point to real code.
cards.when: After creating or modifying aspects, or when paradigm doctor reports stale anchors.

cards.name: paradigm_purpose_validate
cards.description: Validate .purpose files and portal.yaml structural integrity. Checks for missing fields, invalid references, and formatting issues.
cards.when: Before committing changes to .purpose files or portal.yaml. Also useful as a CI check.

cards.description: Initialize Paradigm in a project. Creates .paradigm/ directory, config.yaml, and optionally portal.yaml. Auto-detects discipline from project structure.
flags: --quick: Skip slow operations like scan indexing

cards.description: Scan the codebase and rebuild the symbol index. Reads all .purpose files, portal.yaml, and generates navigator.yaml for fast lookups.
flags: --fix: Attempt to auto-fix minor issues found during scan

cards.description: Validate consistency between Paradigm files and the codebase. Reports errors (broken references), warnings (stale anchors), and info (pending tags).
flags: --json: Output results as JSON for CI integration

cards.description: Synchronize Paradigm files with the current codebase state. Updates navigator.yaml, refreshes indexes, and reconciles any drift.
flags: --dry-run: Show what would be synced without making changes
--force: Overwrite local changes with indexed state

cards.description: View and manage production incidents, failure patterns, and system health metrics. The operational intelligence dashboard.
flags: --status <status>: Filter by incident status (open, investigating, resolved)

cards.description: AI-coordinated multi-agent execution. Analyzes the task, selects agents, plans stages, and executes with handoffs between agents.
flags: --compare: A/B test solo vs faceted approach

cards.description: Spawn a single agent with a specific role (architect, builder, tester, reviewer, security) for a focused task.
flags: --model <model>: Override the default model for this agent

cards.description: Configure MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration. Sets up the paradigm-mcp binary for Claude Code, Cursor, or other MCP-compatible clients.
Promote a suggested tag to the project section of tags.yaml. Part of the governance workflow where humans approve AI-suggested tags.
flags: --to core: Promote to core section instead of project
--reject: Reject and remove the suggested tag

cards.name: [feature]
cards.description: Marks a component as a user-facing feature.

cards.name: [integration]
cards.description: Marks a component as an external service integration. Often paired with the service name.

cards.name: [state]
cards.description: Marks a component as a state management unit.

cards.name: [critical]
cards.description: Marks a symbol as critical-path — failure here causes significant user or business impact. Triggers extra scrutiny in reviews and orchestration.

cards.name: [security]
cards.description: Marks a symbol as security-relevant. Components, aspects, or gates with this tag should involve the security agent during orchestration.

cards.name: [compliance]
cards.description: Marks a symbol as compliance-related (GDPR, SOC2, PCI, etc.). Often paired with [security] on aspects that enforce regulatory requirements.

cards.name: [deprecated]
cards.description: Marks a symbol as deprecated — still functional but scheduled for removal. AI agents should suggest alternatives when encountering deprecated symbols.

cards.name: [idea]
cards.description: Marks a symbol as experimental or in the ideation phase. Not yet approved for production use.

cards.name: Adding a Feature
steps: 1. Call paradigm_orchestrate_inline({ task: '...', mode: 'plan' }) if 3+ files involved
2. Call paradigm_navigate({ intent: 'context', task: '...' }) to discover relevant files
3. Check paradigm_wisdom_context for related symbols
4. If adding API endpoints: call paradigm_gates_for_route for gate suggestions
5. Update portal.yaml with new routes and gates (if applicable)
6. Implement the feature code
7. Create/update the nearest .purpose file with #component and [feature] tag
8. Add !signals for events and $flows for multi-step processes
9. Record implementation with paradigm_history_record
10. Commit with Paradigm format: type(#symbol): description + Symbols: trailer

cards.name: Adding an API Endpoint
steps: 1. Call paradigm_gates_for_route({ route: '/api/...', method: 'POST' })
2. Add the route to portal.yaml with the suggested gates
3. Implement the endpoint with gate enforcement in middleware
4. Add #component to the nearest .purpose file
5. Test that unauthorized access returns 403
6. Commit with the route and gate symbols in the Symbols: trailer

cards.name: Before Modifying a Symbol
steps: 1. Call paradigm_ripple({ symbol: '#target', depth: 2 }) to check impact
2. Call paradigm_wisdom_context({ symbols: ['#target'] }) for team knowledge
3. Call paradigm_history_fragility({ symbols: ['#target'] }) for stability warnings
4. If fragility is HIGH: review paradigm_history_context for recent changes
5. Read the source file only after completing discovery steps
6. After changes: record with paradigm_history_record and update .purpose files

cards.name: Starting a New Session
steps: 1. Call paradigm_session_recover to load breadcrumbs from previous sessions
2. Call paradigm_status for project overview and health
3. Read .paradigm/config.yaml for project discipline and conventions
4. Check if portal.yaml exists (for gate-protected projects)
5. Use paradigm_navigate with 'context' intent for your specific task

cards.name: Preparing a Handoff
steps: 1. Call paradigm_context_check to confirm handoff is recommended
2. Finish or checkpoint the current task
3. Call paradigm_handoff_prepare with: summary, modifiedFiles, symbolsTouched, nextSteps, openQuestions
4. Inform the user of the handoff file location
5. In the new session: call paradigm_session_recover to pick up where you left off
